note_tweet.text:
Perplexity launched Teammates, always-on agents that keep working on a project instead of finishing one task and stopping.

What you get:
- Each agent runs on its own virtual machine with a desktop and a browser.
- Progress shows up in separate threads in the Perplexity app.
- You can talk to them through Slack.
- Only on the Max plan, at $200 a month.

Here's where it sits against similar products:
- Anthropic Duet: from $20
- OpenAI Dots: from $100
- Perplexity Teammates: $200

That's a 10x price spread for always-on agents within about a month.

The entry price doesn't tell you much on its own. An always-on agent burns compute all day, so the cheaper plans will probably hit usage limits fast. SpaceX already tightened limits on Grok Bots because of heavy agent usage.

Before paying for any of these, I'd check:
1. How much work you get before hitting the limit, not just the monthly price.
2. What the agent can access: read-only, or can it send, post and buy.
3. Whether you can see a log of everything it did while you weren't watching.

Which one would you pay for, and what would you have it do all day?
